standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality
standard_prerequisites.statement: A homotopy between two dependent functions yields an equality of the functions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what identifies f = g with the type of pointwise equalities at source line 183.

standard_prerequisites.name: Preservation of n-types under equivalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: If X is equivalent to an n-type, so is X.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at source line 183 after the path space has been replaced by a product of path spaces.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractible dependent products
standard_prerequisites.statement: A dependent product of contractible types is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the base case n = -2 at source line 178.

core_obligations: Induct on n, with the case n = -2 discharged by the corresponding result for dependent products of contractible types (source lines 177-178).
In the step, assume the statement for n-types and that every B(a) is an (n+1)-type; fix f, g : prd a:A B(a) and show that f = g is an n-type (source lines 180-182).
Replace f = g by the product prd a:A (f(a) = g(a)) using function extensionality and closure of n-types under equivalence (source line 183).
Apply the inductive hypothesis to the product, since each f(a) = g(a) is an n-type by assumption (source line 184).

proof_roadmap.step: Base case n = -2 by the contractibility of dependent products.
Induction step: fix two dependent functions and reduce to their path space.
Use function extensionality to rewrite the path space as a product and conclude by the inductive hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.9 at source lines 171-174: if every B(a) is an n-type then prd x:A B(x) is an n-type, for arbitrary A. The proof (source lines 176-185) is an induction whose step is not a direct application of the hypothesis: to show that f = g is an n-type one must first pass from the identity type of two dependent functions to the product prd a:A (f(a) = g(a)), which uses function extensionality (source line 183), and then apply closure under equivalence before the inductive hypothesis can be used on the pointwise path spaces (line 184). The base case at line 178 is a separate input, and the statement itself says nothing about how the path space of a function type is to be rewritten.
